What’s available today?
What this preview shows

Original TrustinJr artwork and recordings in an adapted browser interface. All questions and responses are prepared. The Moon preference is a website illustration, not a native topic category. It changes only the Moon sample; other activities keep their place. No microphone, live AI, device connection, or real child profile is involved. Website privacy

Parent Dock · iPhone

A closer look.
At your side.

01 / Today

A clear view.
Of their day.

Choose a child. Choose a time window. See the activities that have been saved.

Why it’s designed this way

The child selector stays close to the information it controls. Date ranges and the last successful update make the numbers interpretable: whose activity, over which period, and how fresh it is. The native app also clears the old child’s state when switching profiles, so a delayed response cannot quietly show the wrong child’s information.

These are activity counts, not scores or proof of learning. Offline discovery listening is not included. An update time is not a claim of continuous monitoring.

02 / Together

A small moment.
Back to you.

A recent discovery becomes an invitation to talk, notice, or try something together.

Why it’s designed this way

“A moment together” is grounded in a saved activity. Its “Why this suggestion?” view makes that connection explicit. Inviting a child to explain an idea in their own words can help a parent hear what made sense and where a little support would be useful. The design brings the experience back into a human relationship.

A conversation starter is not an assessment of ability, a diagnosis, or an inference about your child’s personality.

03 / Activity

See the exchange.
Keep the context.

Review saved questions and answers. See when a safeguard shaped a response. Delete an individual activity.

Why it’s designed this way

A summary can be useful; the underlying exchange gives it meaning. Activity filters help a parent find Ask, Math, Stories, or safeguard interventions. Details can include the original question, answer, supported versus independent Math practice, and a recorded policy reason. Deletion asks for confirmation and should only leave the detail screen after it succeeds.

Reports cover saved events, not every offline experience. A safeguard notice describes an intervention; it is not an emergency alert or a promise that everything was detected.

04 / Topics

Your family.
Your guidance.

Choose an age-appropriate explanation, a grown-up conversation, or no discussion for supported topics.

Why it’s designed this way

Readiness and family values are contextual. The current iOS source has preferences for religion, violence, non-explicit body development, drugs and alcohol, clean profanity explanations, politics and civics, and money and product literacy. Each choice is named by its consequence. Essential protections remain separate, so a preference cannot authorize harmful instructions, exploitation, or commercial persuasion.

Expanded controls depend on service support and still require release validation. Questions about being hurt or feeling unsafe must retain supportive guidance toward a trusted adult.

05 / Reading

Set a pace.
Let the story breathe.

Hear a reading-speed sample before sending your choice to the paired Watch.

Why it’s designed this way

The parent can listen before deciding. Calm is the starting speed. The native app distinguishes “Saved here. Waiting for the paired Watch.” from “Applied on the paired Watch.” That difference matters: a tap on the phone is not proof that a device has received a setting. Downloaded books remain available offline; they do not require daily reapproval.

This website tour does not send settings to a device. Its separate interactive audio preview uses prepared recordings.

06 / Guidance

A useful foothold.
Room to grow.

Set the starting math level and choose a supported explanation style.

Why it’s designed this way

A starting level is a place to begin, not a permanent label. The current source includes age and starting Math controls, with difficulty adapting as practice continues. Bounded guidance choices—shorter sentences, familiar everyday examples, or avoiding scary imagery—make the requested support understandable. Existing progress is preserved rather than reset to a new-profile default.

TrustinJr initially focuses on ages 4–5. Wider age choices in development source are not an announcement of broader release support. Illustrated books keep their fixed wording; no learning gains are promised.

07 / Watch setup

Connected.
On your terms.

Choose a child, prepare the connection, and send it to the paired Watch.

Why it’s designed this way

Setup separates a parent account, a child profile, and a Watch’s access. The device list states access expiry instead of pretending the Watch is currently online. Disconnect asks for confirmation and explains its scope: it stops future server access, without unpairing Apple devices or deleting the parent account. Watch-face customization remains an optional destination.

The current beta requires a Watch normally paired with this iPhone. Apple Family Setup is not supported in this beta. Master Guardian sharing is a separate, unfinished account-design direction and is not presented as available here.
